text: Say Yes to the Dress is an American reality television series on TLC that follows events at Kleinfeld Bridal in Manhattan, showcasing the work of individual sales associates, managers, and fitters, as well as profiling brides as they search for their perfect wedding dress. Common themes include overwhelming advice from friends and family, the role of the "perfect dress" in helping brides overcome personal challenges, struggles with weight and body image, and the difficulty of staying within budget—particularly when purchasing dresses by Kleinfeld’s exclusive designer, Pnina Tornai. Dresses featured on the show range from $1,300 to $40,000. Mara Urshel is one of the co-owners of Kleinfeld; she previously served as senior vice president and general merchandise manager at Saks Fifth Avenue for twenty years, and later held executive positions at Casual Corner and Geoffrey Beene Company. She co-purchased the Kleinfeld Bridal store with Ronald Rothstein and Wayne Rogers on July 9, 1999. Ronald (Ronnie) Rothstein is another co-owner; he graduated from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania in 1964 and earned his law degree from the University of Miami in 1968, becoming a member of the Florida Bar. He founded Oh Dawn in 1976, which he sold after eight years to an American Stock Exchange company, remaining in an executive role for several more years. He also co-purchased Kleinfeld on July 9, 1999, with Mara Urshel and Wayne Rogers. Randy Fenoli served as the Fashion Director at Kleinfeld; born in Mt. Vernon, Illinois, he began sewing dresses at age nine and later worked in makeup artistry, hair styling, and entertainment before enrolling at New York’s Fashion Institute of Technology. He was hired by Paul Diamond of The Diamond Collection and then joined Kleinfeld, where he worked until 2012, after which he became an independent consultant. Dorothy Silver is the Director of Sales and Merchandising at Kleinfeld, having started her career as a floor manager at Bonwit Teller and spent most of her twenty-five-year retail career at Kleinfeld, working with Nicole Sacco and Joan Roberts. Nicole Sacco is the Director of Fittings and Sales at Kleinfeld, having worked there for thirteen years, primarily assisting consultants with client needs such as dress selection, closing sales, or ensuring client satisfaction, and she works with Dorothy Silver and Joan Roberts. Nitsa Glezelis is the Director of Alterations at Kleinfeld, born in Kos, Greece, and having worked in retail since age twelve; she has been at Kleinfeld for eighteen years and works with Vera Skenderis. Joan Roberts is the Director of Sales/Bridal Manager at Kleinfeld, with twenty-five years of retail experience prior to joining Kleinfeld, and she works with Nicole Sacco and Dorothy Silver. Camille Coffey is a bridal consultant at Kleinfeld who first visited the store while shopping for a dress to wear to her son’s wedding, applied for a job, and has worked there since. Vera Skenderis is the Alterations Manager at Kleinfeld, born in Athens, Greece, and with thirty-four years of retail experience, working alongside Nitsa Glezelis. Audrey Pisani is a bridal consultant born in Brooklyn who has worked in retail for twenty years, fifteen of which have been in bridal wear. Keasha Rigsby is a bridal consultant with fifteen years of retail experience, six of which have been in bridal wear; she first encountered Kleinfeld while shopping with her cousin, met co-owner Ronnie Rothstein, applied for a job, and has worked there since. She has not appeared on Say Yes to the Dress since the January 2011 season and will appear on a new show, Keasha's Perfect Dress, on the Canadian Slice network, which will follow her as she opens a new bridal salon. Debbie Asprea is a bridal consultant with eighteen years of retail experience, fifteen of which have been spent at Kleinfeld, and she credits her love of fashion to her father, a dress contractor.
